dublinCore.title: Phase Spectrum: What the Magnitude Hides
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Phase spectrum
Magnitude spectrum
Discrete Fourier transform
Time shift
Linear phase
Phase unwrapping
dublinCore.description: Three views of the phase spectrum. A: three harmonics with fixed amplitudes and adjustable phases change shape and peak while the magnitude spectrum and RMS stay fixed. B: a time shift tau turns the phase spectrum of a pulse or sawtooth into a line of slope -2 pi tau (100-point DFT, wrapped or unwrapped). C: a 256-point DFT swap experiment rebuilds signals from the magnitude of one and the phase of another, with zero-phase and phase-only variants.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Explain why signals with identical magnitude spectra can have very different waveforms and peak values
Identify phases that grow linearly with frequency, phi_k = k phi_1, as a pure time delay tau = -phi_1 / (360 degrees f0)
Calculate the phase -2 pi f tau added by a delay tau and the interval 1/|tau| at which the wrapped phase repeats
Distinguish 2 pi wrapping jumps from pi jumps caused by sign changes of a real spectrum
Analyze the swap experiment to conclude that the timing of a signal's features is carried by its phase
prerequisites: The DFT and the magnitude spectrum

misconceptions.misconception: The magnitude spectrum describes the signal; the phase is a minor detail
misconceptions.correction: Phase sets how the components line up in time, so it determines the waveform's shape, peak and the timing of its features
misconceptions.evidence: View A keeps |X| fixed while the peak moves between 1.44 and 1.83; in view C, |A| with the phase of B resembles B (r = 0.64)

misconceptions.misconception: Every jump in a phase plot is a 2 pi wrap
misconceptions.correction: Wrapping jumps are 2 pi and vanish when unwrapped; a real spectrum that changes sign adds jumps of pi that are not part of the delay
misconceptions.evidence: In view B the rectangular pulse's phase jumps from 0 to 180 degrees between 9 and 10 Hz at tau = 0, and the unwrapped phase climbs by pi at each sign change

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Phase spectrum explorer with three views chosen by radio buttons. View A: three harmonics with fixed amplitudes and phase sliders; the waveform changes shape while the magnitude bars stay fixed. View B: a pulse or sawtooth is delayed by tau and its phase spectrum becomes a straight line of slope -2 pi tau, shown wrapped or unwrapped. View C: two signals A and B are rebuilt from the magnitude of one and the phase of the other, and each rebuilt signal resembles the signal that supplied its phase.

visualElements.description: View A: waveform x(t) over two periods with the all-zero-phase reference, plus magnitude bars (maroon) and phase bars (green) for the three harmonics
View B: delayed signal with a tau arrow, normalised magnitude stems and phase dots with the line of slope -2 pi tau, wrapped or unwrapped, and a frequency cursor
View C: four stacked time plots (A, B and two rebuilt signals) with correlation read-outs r_A and r_B
Read-outs: peak and RMS (A); slope -2 pi tau, wrap interval and cursor |X| and phase (B); r_A, r_B and zero-phase peak time (C)

model.description: A: x(t) = sum_k A_k cos(2 pi k f0 t + phi_k) with A_k = 1, 1/2, 1/3 and f0 = 1 Hz. B: a 100-sample signal (fs = 100 Hz) is circularly shifted by tau and transformed with a DFT; bins with |X| < 0.1% of the maximum have undefined phase. C: two 256-sample signals are transformed and rebuilt by the inverse DFT from |X1| e^{j angle X2}, |X| alone, or e^{j angle X}.
equations: x(t - tau) <-> X(f) e^{-j 2 pi f tau}
slope of phase = -2 pi tau rad/Hz
algorithms: Direct DFT and inverse DFT (N = 100 and N = 256)
Phase unwrapping by adding multiples of 2 pi between neighbouring defined bins
limitations: Shifts are circular and in whole samples (0.01 s)
Unwrapping cannot remove the pi jumps of a real spectrum that changes sign
Phase is undefined (set to 0 in view C) where |X| is below 0.1% of its maximum

instructionalStrategies: Predict the waveform from the phases before pressing a preset
Read the phase at a cursor frequency and compute the delay
Predict which original a swapped reconstruction resembles
extensions: Add a user-drawn signal to the swap experiment
Show group delay as the negative derivative of the unwrapped phase
